assumptions: The disputeToken is a fee-on-transfer token as configured by the governor.
The user's disputeTree() deposit is a legitimate use, not a malicious attack.
resolveDispute() is the only function that clears the disputer and enables tree updates.

limitations: Only the resolveDispute() revert impact is formalized; disputer-stuck, tree-update blocking, and recovery failure are separate impacts not covered here.
The completion obligation is represented as a grounded Boolean because the report states the success/revert outcome without a numeric transfer formula.
The impact is formalized as the absence of the blocked-tree-updates condition under the stated deposit scenario; the underlying balance arithmetic is not numerically bound.
The report does not specify the exact mechanism linking resolveDispute() revert to tree publication/revocation, so the relation is kept at the report-stated observable level.
